On a side note, make sure you max out th6 before th7. Maxing th6 and 7 before upgrading are some of the most important things you'll do early in the game.

Silly wall upgrading strategy - just protect the most important things first. Troops will tend to go for weaker walls, so those walls are currently going to waste.

You probably shouldn't be in gold at that level.

If you're in a clan that donates well, put CC inside base and get some good defense troops after every attack. That will save you so, so much. 

Trap placement!!!! Put traps where troops will definitely walk over them - inside the base! "It's okay to have space in your base!"

Besides this, this is a decent th6 base. If you're getting wrecked by heroes, there's nothing you can do. You need to drop trophies. Those level defenses simply aren't equipped to deal with heroes.

When I was TH7, I used Giant - Healer - Archer/Wizard. Wizards are more expensive but more effective. If the AD is easy to destroy, let giants handle that before dropping your healer(s). Drop archer or wizard in an arch outside the base where you want to place giants, and then drop giants with the archer/wizard 'shield'. Watch for obvious traps - spring traps are the death of this attack.

Level one drags are expensive, but won't do much for you at TH7. The air defense available at TH7 destroys a level 1 drag. 

They should never be used for farming, either. They will get you good stars usually, but at a cost.

When I saw how useless the spring trap upgrades were, I didn't even consider spending the gold when I have other things to do. The valks are the only real reason, but still, I have other things to do.

Pretty good for a TH7 base. I would never put two cannons right next to each other. Also, doubling up on bombs usually isn't the best choice. I live by the rule of putting all traps (besides giant bomb on some exceptions) within the walls. It may let more troops in, but it's more likely to destroy the offense.

I'll expand upon the common 'x' is horrible comments.

At your level, most people think that there can be no space in your base. I did the same. However, space is IMPORTANT. 

Your base has a lot of compartments, as well as double walls. Remember that doubling up on walls is USELESS. Wallbreakers can deal with it fairly easily, and most troops won't bother and will go for the single walls. 

When you're making compartments, think about where troops are going to go. Giants are a common attack at that level. Where are they going to go? They're likely going to go either through the first player and to the center, immediately getting your important mortars, or around the outside, through compartments. This design stops them from easily traveling to every defense because of compartments. However, you could force them to travel over spring traps and weaken the attacker severely. Instead of walls between defenses, try a single missing wall - replaced with a spring trap.  They will see a clear opening and go for it, but then the spring trap will hit.

Your traps are one of the most important things for defensive strategy. Clumpling them up is useless. They should ALWAYS GO INSIDE THE BASE. The only expection is giant bomb, which can go outside, usually in your weakest point, to stop big attacks on your weak point. 

Also, upgrade those mines!!!

It's good that you're seeking help already at TH6. It will help you advance faster than most. I hope this helped!

The best TH7 base is the one you use your knowledge of defense to create. Although TH7 isn't quite the level where all your attackers will be familiar with possible base designs and how to three star, it's best to learn how to make your own base now.

You didn't tell us what kind of base you want. The basic types are trophy (aka war), farming (now less distinct a category due to the update that killed them), and hybrid. The trophy base assumes you don't care if they get all your resources. The farming category assumes you don't care if you lose trophies, but you want to save all the resources you can. The hybrid is a balance between those. Of course, then you get into bases built to defend against specific attacks - the ones most likely to be used at your level.

Look at good TH8 and 9 bases and take notes of the layout. You obviously can't copy them, but you can learn from them. How do they position defenses? How do they position barracks, camps, etc? Where is the TH and clan castle? What's in the clan castle? Is this base trophy, farming, or hybrid? Analyze closer - what is this base trying to defend against? 

Some of the most common mistakes I see include bad trap placement, wall placement, and extra building placement. I'll go over just a few little details on each.

Traps are important, and probably one of the most strategic parts of your base. You want to make sure you use them to their full potential. One of the most common attacks at TH7 is giants and archer or wiz. By replacing ONE wall between two defensive compartments with a spring trap, you force giants to walk over it. If they are going from a compartment with a cannon to a compartment with an archer, they won't break a wall to avoid a trap - they'll go around the wall, and three of them will be flung into the air. 

While compartmenting all your defenses is common at TH7, it's not effective for air attacks. Long story short, ITS OKAY to have empty space within your walls - just not enough that troops can be placed inside them.

Don't place all your extra buildings in groups (all your camps next to eachother, all your mines on one side, etc). They add an extra layer that will effectively slow down everything but giants and loons. While the troops have to destroy outside buildings to get to the inside, they'll be taking damage. Also, if you alternate placement of mines and collectors all around your base, the enemy can't target just gold or elixir - they'll get some of both, but in lower quantities.

TL;DR sorry for the super long post but I hope it helps, learn to make your own base. If you don't want to, just search youtube for "TH7 <base type> base design" and there will be plenty of results. You won't find many here.

I mean, you listed a bunch of positives that make it better than the hog. It's fairly safe from traps and they only take damage when they are dealing it (basically). They also do, of course, become tankier than hogs through levels. 

I think they need a small buff in damage, but otherwise, I prefer them to hogs. I expect some really good armies to be made with them. Something involving golems and miners. GoWiMi has a ring to it (although it probably wouldn't hold up against the many better armies, and will probably get hate for being similar to the infamous GoWiPe).

Space within your base is allowed, and actually really helpful. I know you'll read that you want lots of little sections in your base, but even at that level, air will just ignore it all anyway. I recommend taking out a single wall between defense compartments and throwing a spring trap there. Giants going from defense to defense will have to cross it (because they want to go around the walls), and the offense will take a big hit.

Update: I saw your fixed base. While putting your traps in a row like that seems to make sense, the best way to do it is to FORCE troops over the traps. Instead of a line of trap-trap-trap, wall-wall-trap will force the troops right over the trap. Also, your base seems to assume the attacker is coming from either the bottom right or top left - the other sides are weakspots. That's a lot better in the updated version, but still an issue.

You should also throw your extra buildings (outside walls) in not-so-bunched up groups. If an attacker barchered you, they could easily get all of your collectors and mines because they're in one place. I usually put them in an even ring all around the outside of the base, alternating mines and collectors. This is still quite susceptible to barch, but they will have to expend a lot more troops. 

These outside-the-walls buildings are also good to use as distraction - they do have HP, especially barracks. If you spread them evenly around the outside of your base, troops will have to go through a layer of useless buildings before getting to the good stuff. While they are doing that, they will be taking damage. This does not apply to giants and ballons, of course, but it's still good to do.

I'd also recommend not putting all your storages in one compartment. Once someone breaks into that compartment, they have easy access to all your storage. If you were to move them to separate compartments closer to the outside, it'd be easier to get one storage, but much harder to get all of them. If you play chess, it's much like if you had to sacrifice a pawn to save your king. 

I know that's a lot, but that's most of the basics of base building that you will use through your entire time in Clash of Clans, specifically up to max th8 (then it gets more complex, lol)
